articles.headline: Labour brings Wales' first dockless e-bike scheme to Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has chosen Voi to run Wales' first dockless e-bike scheme, growing to 500 e-bikes across the city in its first year.
body: Swansea residents will soon be able to pick up an e-bike at any hour of the day or night, as Swansea's Labour council brings the first dockless e-bike scheme in Wales to the city.

Following a competitive tender, the Labour administration has chosen Voi Technology to run the new e-bike rental scheme. It will start with an initial fleet across Swansea University's campuses, city centre locations and key transport hubs, then grow to 500 e-bikes across the city within the first year. The service will run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "It has long been our ambition to have a Swansea-wide e-bike scheme and I'm delighted that we are partnering with Voi. Similar schemes around the UK have quickly become very well used, offering a new form of public transport providing a convenient, affordable, and sustainable travel option for everyday short journeys."

Keeping costs down for residents is built in from the start. Rides start at 50p to unlock and 20p per minute on pay-as-you-go, with day, week and month passes for regular users. The unlock fee will be waived for the scheme's first six months, and every new customer gets their first three 15-minute rides free.

Discounts are available for students, NHS workers, the over 60s, people with disabilities, military personnel and people on low incomes. The fleet will include both Explorer 5 and Explorer Light 2 e-bikes, designed for everyone from daily commuters to first-time riders. The Explorer Light 2 has previously been shown to increase ridership among women and older riders in comparable UK schemes.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said: "I think the bikes will prove very popular with residents both for getting about the city as well as leisure and they will be yet another attraction for visitors to Swansea given we have some of the most expansive and picturesque cycle routes in Wales."

The scheme is designed to link Swansea's universities, city centre, transport hubs and communities. Its early focus is on closing the last-mile gap to places such as Singleton Park and SA1, and on joining up with the Swansea Bay Metro and the Strand hub. The fleet will grow in stages from an initial 70 e-bikes to 200, 350 and then 500, with the ambition to reach as many as 1,500 as demand is proven and in agreement with the council.

It is good news for jobs and for cleaner air too. The e-bikes will be powered with 100% renewable energy and backed by a zero emissions operations fleet, and the scheme will create 18 new jobs as well as apprenticeships in sustainable transport operations.

This is Labour getting things done for Swansea: a long-held ambition turned into a city-wide, affordable travel option that puts Swansea first in Wales, opens up new jobs and helps every resident get where they need to go.

articles.headline: Swansea's Labour council to widen popular NCN4 path between Dunvant and Gowerton
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has secured £500,000 from the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund to upgrade a 1.75km stretch of NCN4 between Dunvant and Gowerton.
body: Swansea's Labour council is pressing ahead with more improvements to one of the city's best-loved walking and cycling routes, with a further section of National Cycle Network 4 (NCN4) set to be upgraded and widened.

The Labour-run council has secured £500,000 through the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund to improve the section of NCN4 between Dunvant and Gowerton. The work will cover a 1.75km stretch, creating a wider, more comfortable and more accessible shared-use path for everyone who walks, wheels or cycles there.

This builds on the council's earlier widening and resurfacing work on NCN4 between Blackpill and Dunvant. Those improvements have been well received and have already helped improve access, safety and capacity on the popular Clyne Valley route.

NCN4 is one of Swansea's key active travel routes. It links communities including Gowerton, Dunvant, Killay and Blackpill, with onward connections towards Mumbles, Swansea city centre and neighbouring areas. The upgrade will give pedestrians, cyclists and people using mobility aids more room to pass each other, easing congestion and making the route better for commuters, families, leisure users and visitors alike.

Cllr Andrew Stevens, Swansea Council's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, said: "This is another important investment in Swansea's active travel network and will build on the improvements already delivered between Blackpill and Dunvant."

He added: "By widening the path we can make it more comfortable, accessible and attractive for all users, giving people more space and helping to support safer journeys on foot, by bike and by other active travel means."

Some sections of the route will need to close temporarily while the work takes place, and users are asked to follow local signage and plan ahead during construction. Cllr Stevens said: "We appreciate that temporary closures will cause some disruption while the work is taking place, but these are needed to allow the improvements to be delivered safely. We will keep disruption to a minimum and make sure clear information is available for route users."
The Welsh Government's Regional Transport Fund supports transport investment across Wales, with a strong focus on walking, wheeling, cycling and public transport improvements.
This is Labour delivering step by step for Swansea: safer, greener and more accessible ways to get around, connecting our communities and making everyday journeys better for residents of all ages.
articles.sourceTitle: Popular Swansea walking and cycle route to be upgraded
